newsitem.title: JAPAN: MOF unveils reform ideas, but no concrete plan.
newsitem.headline: MOF unveils reform ideas, but no concrete plan.

text.p: Finance Minister Wataru Kubo on Wednesday unveiled the basic principles of a plan to reform the ministry, but said concrete steps will be worked out later.
In a news conference, Kubo made public the results of a review of the ministry's structure which a task force of ministry bureaucrats has been conducting since April.
The ministry came under fire for its handling of problems in the banking industry and has been urged to change its practice of trying to deal with banking crises internally.
"As a result of the review, we have come up with three principles...and we would like to work out details of the reform plans as soon as possible after the elections," Kubo said.
A senior coalition official said earlier that general elections would be held soon.
Under the principles, the ministry will strengthen its inspections of the financial industry.

"While keeping a tense relationship between the inspection function of the MOF and the supervisory function, the two sides also need to cooperate sufficiently when needed," Kubo said, leaving unclear the ministry's view on a widely debated issue of separating the inspection function from the ministry.
The review also called for the ministry to study the possibility of reorganising its structure according to functions performed, rather than having various departments conducting similar functions.
Kubo also said the ministry will minimise its guidance of financial institutions.
"I don't think the principles unveiled today are enough. The ministry will be appraised on how serious it is about its own reforms when it presents specific reform plans," Kubo said.
The three parties in Japan's ruling coalition have said they will map out their own outline plans for reform of the ministry by Thursday.
Kubo said the coalition plan will be taken into account when the ministry works on specific plans of its own.
